You have two options:

1. **Run this in Claude Code on the machine that has the recording.** It can use a speech-to-text engine already on your machine, or install one if you agree first, then transcribe the recording there. It will ask which language you spoke, and if you want each line tagged with who spoke, it can try to separate the voices and ask you who each one is. It then writes a file the debrief can upload.

2. **Use a transcription tool you already have,** as long as it can export exactly this format. Each line has one timestamp from the start of the session, one speaker (the person, not their character) and what they said:

```text
[00:01:10] GM: The causeway runs out across the salt marsh.
[00:02:20] Sam: I bet she works for the raiders.
```

The timestamps can never go backwards from one line to the next. The file must be UTF-8, under 8 MB and at most 20,000 lines. Most tools export SRT or VTT instead, and the upload rejects those. Claude Code can convert them to this format first.

Once you have the file, bring it back and we'll start the debrief.
